verdict.reasoning: Patient states knees are hurting and clicking and expresses concern: "my knees are hurting and they're clicking a lot and it's starting to worry me."
Duration: "probably it's been about two weeks." Side and trigger: later clarifies "It's actually my right knee that hurts" and pain starts "after maybe 20 minutes or so" of running.
She reports clicking with flexion/extension when doing abdominal exercises: "when I do my abs, it kind of requires me to... flex... and straighten my legs. Then I hear all this clicking."
She links worse pain with longer runs: "I can't run very far anymore without just feeling pain in my knees" and notes pain starting after ~20 minutes of running; she is doing longer runs (7–8 miles).

She describes transient swelling post-run that responds to ice and is absent now: "the first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen, but then I just put some, like, ice on it and it went away. But right now... it's not swollen."
She reports a single episode: "there was this tingling in my toes... on my right toes" and later: "it was just that time, but it was just really weird" indicating it did not persist.

Instability/locking/ROM/stairs/walking all denied: "Not that. I mean, it just kind of starts hurting" (re instability), "Any locking up... ?" "No." "Any problems going up and down stairs?" "No." "Any problems just walking normally?" "No, I don't." "are you able to fully straighten... fully flex it?" "Yes... Yes."

Left knee: "Any problems with your left one?" "No." But she does report other joint/limb issues: intermittent leg swelling and prior joint issues: "sometimes I have some joint issues" and swelling in legs/feet with sock indentation, so saying "no other joint pain or swelling" is inaccurate.

She mentions a fall and bruise but does not specify it was to the knee: "I play some ice hockey and I had this injury a few months ago... had a huge bruise." No location of the bruise is given, so "to the knee" is added detail.

Asthma and allergies are not discussed; GI issues are asked: "any problems with your stomach or asthma, indigestion?" and she answers "No problems." No explicit statement about allergies is made, so claiming "reports no allergies" adds information.
"I do have. I'm farsighted" directly supports this.
She states: "I had LASIK surgery."
She describes a "really bad uti" and ER visit: "they had me actually in er" but no explicit statement of formal hospitalization (admission) is made, so "required hospitalization" is an extrapolation.
She uses ibuprofen intermittently: "I take ibuprofen and I'll just kind of use it sometime... maybe like 400 milligrams max."

She is unsure: "I'll take like, ibuprofen or actually acetamin. I'll take. What am I taking? Aleve. Whatever Aleve is. I think that's maybe setaminophen." This is ambiguous, not a clear statement that she takes acetaminophen as a separate medication; documenting it as a distinct medication is added certainty.
She states: "I'll take... Aleve. Whatever Aleve is."
"I take vitamin D."
"I take melatonin sometimes" supports this.
"Occasionally if I'm really having hard times... sleeping, I'll take Xanax."
Allergies are never mentioned in the transcript, so stating "Patient reports no allergies" introduces new information rather than reflecting a documented denial.
She is training for a marathon and increased to 7–8 mile runs: "I'm currently training for a marathon... maybe like seven or eight miles" and notes she started with 4–5 miles about a month ago.
She says: "I go to the gym like three times a week."
She reports: "I also sometimes will, you know, smoke a joint." This supports occasional cannabis use.

She reports no current swelling and full ROM; no redness mentioned and specifically denied inflammatory signs in legs: "right now it's not swollen"; "Yes" to full flexion/extension; later denies color/temperature changes in lower legs: "Nope."
The encounter is a video/phone consult with no documented physical exam maneuvers or findings by the clinician; assessment and plan are based on history only.

Symptoms summarized accurately (right knee exertional pain, clicking, prior minor trauma). The clinician notes likely injury and possible cartilage problem: "injuries..." and suggests imaging "to have a look inside the knee and see if there's any problem with the cartilage," consistent with overuse vs internal derangement consideration.

The tingling episode is clearly acknowledged in the history and is part of the overall assessment discussion: "another weird thing... tingling in my toes... it was just that time" and the clinician later asks about its resolution: "has that gone back to normal now?"
Clinician advises: "definitely carrying on with the ice therapy that you've been using... as much as you can use the ice."

Running modification: "I would try and ease up on the running if you can. And if it's painful enough that you're having to stop running, then it's not a good idea to do that." This implies reducing/pausing when pain recurs.
Clinician: "I can prescribe you a slightly stronger anti inflammatory that you can take regularly instead of the ibuprofen, but not with the ibuprofen, but make sure that with food."
Same quote: "instead of the ibuprofen, but not with the ibuprofen" instructs to avoid dual NSAID use.
Clinician: "the best thing, I would suggest getting an appointment with the physiotherapist first" and later confirms: "Yeah, for that" (re referral).
Imaging is contingent: "then make an assessment as to whether we need to do any imagery to have a look inside the knee and see if there's any problem with the cartilage."

Safety-netting: "If in the meantime you develop like persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee or high temperature, feel unwell, or it completely locks up and you can't bend and stretch it, then you'd need to see a doctor urgently. So call us back in that case."
